          Causal Analysis for a
            Universal Bank
A Shared Scientific Library and Independent Product
Longitudinal inference, econometric panels, partial observation,
    causal discovery and the organization of banking data



                 Research and product proposal

                        7 October 2026
                          Version 2.0
Prologue

A deposit campaign appears successful when balances rise among customers who receive an
offer. Yet those customers may already have been about to move money into the bank. A
collections intervention may improve repayments this month while changing who remains
eligible for assistance next month. A new branch policy may coincide with a local economic
recovery. Each situation requires an answer about an intervention, a population and a period
of time.
   The banking group has much of the raw information needed to investigate these questions.
It also has many useful statistical libraries. What it commonly lacks is a reliable way
to preserve the meaning of an analysis as it moves between data preparation, estimation,
policy comparison and another application. A customer identifier changes; a feature uses a
revised balance unavailable at the decision; a treatment is recorded as acceptance rather than
assignment; an estimator returns an effect whose population differs from the business case.
These are scientific and product failures at the same time.
  This proposal develops a common platform around that problem. It begins with bank
decisions, derives identifying conditions and estimators, evaluates available software, and
specifies the data and evidence that components must exchange. Large-scale computation
executes a valid study. Partial observation remains a modeling and identification problem.
Causal discovery proposes and constrains explanations under explicit assumptions.
   The product develops three workspaces together: policy and transmission, sequential
decisions with controlled latent-state estimation, and temporal discovery with automatic data
organization. They share an auditable account of information, interventions and financial
outcomes. Their scientific qualification is explicit: an identified effect, a conditional model
scenario and an ambiguous graph are distinct useful outputs.
  The argument proceeds from identification and estimator derivation through complete
synthetic banking studies to data construction, software selection and an equal-output invest-
ment comparison. The studies fit unknown models, retain unfavorable results and separate
numerical verification from bank validation. The product earns its common construction cost
only through measured reuse or additional decision value relative to expert composition.
  The evidence cutoff is 7 October 2026. The accompanying archive preserves 87 scholarly
PDFs, three official guidance documents, a dated census of 44 open-source projects, reading
notes, discovery records and source hashes. The survey is a reproducible purposive review
with explicit access and coverage limits. It is not an exhaustive systematic review. Numerical
evidence includes exact checks, fitted synthetic banking studies, repeated-sample experiments
and bounded component measurements; it does not measure bank performance. This is an
author-reviewed proposal and reusable specifications; it does not claim a deployed product,
independent validation or institutional endorsement.

           Part I

Bank decisions and scientific
       foundations




              1
Chapter 1

The bank decision and the product

1.1     An intervention has an economic meaning

Consider a bank deciding whether to offer a temporary savings-rate enhancement to households
at risk of withdrawing funds. The action is the assigned offer, including its rate, duration,
communication channel and eligibility rules. Acceptance is a subsequent event. The outcome
is incremental discounted relationship contribution over a declared horizon, including funding
value, interest expense, servicing cost and transfers from the bank’s other products. A positive
effect on the promoted account’s balance need not imply a positive effect on the banking
group’s value.
  The study must distinguish externally acquired funds, retained funds and internal transfers.
A customer who moves money from another group account changes the product manager’s
balance without necessarily creating new funding. Discounting, funds-transfer pricing and
capital allocation belong to an explicit valuation specification. They are not quantities a
causal estimator should invent. The treatment-effect output includes a currency, valuation
date, horizon, population and contrast direction.
  This running example has empirical roots. Deposit pricing and monetary transmission
vary with local market structure (Drechsler et al., 2017); bank relationships exhibit persistent
cross-selling patterns whose interpretation requires a design distinguishing stickiness from
preferences (Basten and Juelsrud, 2026). Those studies inform mechanisms and designs. Their
coefficients are not transferable estimates of a new bank’s campaign.



1.2     Four scientific routes, one shared record

The product should make four routes available within a common study record. An experiment
or adjustment study asks how a specified action changes an outcome when assignment is
randomized or conditionally exchangeable. A panel study exploits a policy change across entities
and dates, with its own counterfactual trend or instrument restrictions. A sequential study
compares strategies whose earlier actions alter later information and eligibility. A discovery
study investigates graph structure under stated assumptions and returns the appropriate
equivalence class or structural hypothesis.
   These routes share entity definitions, clocks, outcome components, lineage and evidence.
They do not share a universal identification theorem. A graph inferred from transactions cannot
automatically validate an instrument; an accurate hidden-state filter cannot automatically
validate a treatment policy. The central object is a study specification: a versioned statement of

the decision, information set, target population, causal contrast, design assumptions, estimator,
uncertainty and acceptable use.

Table 1.1: Proposed applications. Valid identifying variation must be established within the
bank.

   Banking research demonstrates why different routes are needed. Agarwal et al. (2020)
exploit refinancing-program eligibility rather than simply comparing borrowers who refinance
with those who do not. Mian and Khwaja (2006) compare lending by differently affected banks
to the same firm to separate borrower demand from bank liquidity supply. Benetton (2021)
combine mortgage demand and lender behavior to analyze market-wide regulation. Beraja
et al. (2019) explain why regional refinancing responses alone cannot determine aggregate
policy effects. These are economically meaningful designs, not interchangeable regression
templates.


1.3     What the independent product sells
The standalone offering is a workbench for bank economists, decision scientists and model
owners. A user defines a study, builds a population as of a decision date, examines support
and design diagnostics, runs declared estimators and challengers, and exports an evidence
package for a decision meeting. The package connects a financial recommendation to data,
assumptions, results and limitations. An API offers the same operations to other applications.
   The product has three substantive workspaces from the outset of development. The policy
and transmission workspace analyzes interventions across customer panels, branches and
macroeconomic dates. The sequential decision workspace estimates longitudinal effects and
controlled latent-state models, then compares policies using the information actually available
to their decision maker. The discovery and data workspace reconstructs temporal datasets and
investigates candidate mechanisms under explicit structural restrictions. These are the central
requested capabilities. Campaign effects are one application of the scientific core.
   The workspaces have different qualification levels within each release. For example, a first
release can provide useful finite-state POMDP estimation and model-conditional scenarios
while withholding an unsupported claim to identify a historical intervention. A discovery result
4                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


can be a useful PAG or a ranked experiment proposal without becoming a unique directed
causal graph. The build sequence develops these capabilities together with the data foundation;
it does not defer the central scientific problems to an unspecified later product.
   The library owns study compilation, temporal transformations, adapter contracts, uncer-
tainty aggregation, graph semantics, evidence export and validation. It should reuse established
estimators rather than reproduce their entire implementations. The independent product adds
workspaces, collaboration within bank systems, study search, controlled access and operational
support. Both forms invoke the same scientific core.


1.4      A testable differentiation claim

The strongest alternative is an expert team composing its warehouse, catalog, notebooks and
existing causal packages. That team can already perform excellent analyses. The proposed
product earns its cost only if it reduces repeated data and review work, catches consequential
errors earlier, and increases the number of usable studies without weakening scientific standards.
   Evaluation should compare matched studies with that alternative: analyst time, time
to reconstruct another analyst’s result, frequency of decision-time leakage, material review
findings, compute cost and the value of decisions supported. A polished graph display or faster
fitting is insufficient. The incremental value must be measured against what the same experts
could achieve with existing tools.
   The defensible assets are banking temporal semantics, reusable financial outcome definitions,
accepted study patterns, and evidence that travels between applications. A proprietary
estimator collection is less compelling given the available open-source ecosystem.


1.5      Institutional setting

A universal bank is not one homogeneous dataset. Legal entities, booking locations, currencies,
product systems and access rights constrain analysis. The default deployment brings computa-
tion to approved bank data, exports authorized results, and records the population each result
covers. Cross-border pooling is an explicit design decision. A group-wide report can combine
compatible local estimates without unrestricted movement of transaction records.
   The initial sponsor should be a central analytics or economics function with one retail
product owner and named data owners. Model risk, security and data governance participate
in acceptance. They define permissible use, validate material models, and determine which
artifacts another business unit may rely on. No named banking group is asserted to have
requested or accepted this design.


1.6      The decision system the bank needs

A bank-wide platform must answer questions at several levels. A collections manager compares
assistance strategies for an eligible cohort. A funding team asks how a rate change alters
deposit persistence and the cost of funds. A chief economist estimates transmission across
regions and banking entities. A model-development team asks whether new measurements can
distinguish two causal explanations. The same transaction may support all four questions, but
the interventions, populations and independent units differ.
    The common scientific record therefore has six linked objects. The population records who
1.7. A usable end-to-end research journey                                                      5


was eligible before a decision and preserves later departures. The information set reconstructs
what the actor could know. The intervention identifies assignment, execution, duration and
permissible subsequent actions. The outcome account specifies cash, impairment, funding
and customer outcomes on a dated horizon. The identification argument describes which
features of the observed law determine the requested contrast. The estimate carries uncertainty,
diagnostics and the exact evidence used. Shared storage is useful because these objects travel
together, not because every dataset becomes one table.
   For example, a credit-limit application may consume a treatment-effect estimate from this
library and a cash-flow engine from another repository. The effect might concern utilization
after an assigned limit increase among eligible current cardholders. The valuation engine must
not interpret it as an effect on new-account acceptance or on default among all applicants.
The product checks those declared types and retains the empirical study that supports them.
Human and model review must still examine whether the declared types correctly describe the
bank’s source data. Mechanical compatibility is necessary for composition and insufficient for
truth.


1.7     A usable end-to-end research journey
Suppose a funding economist receives a proposal for a 25-basis-point retention offer. The
first screen asks for the decision, eligible population, comparison policy and outcome horizon.
It displays an observed accounting baseline: balances, external inflows, internal transfers
and interest paid. The economist can inspect the definitions and reconciliation totals before
requesting an effect. A large balance movement with no external funding movement is then
visible before model fitting begins.
   The next step selects a design. A randomized assignment supports an intention- to-treat
analysis. A staggered branch rollout supports a cohort-time comparison only with a defensible
untreated trend. Discretionary account-level offers need measured-history exchangeability or
another identification route. The interface explains the resulting population and comparison
in the language of the funding decision. It does not present these choices as interchangeable
algorithms ranked by predictive accuracy.
   The economist then sees overlap or donor diagnostics, the main estimate, predeclared
alternatives and a financial decomposition. In the executed rollout study in Chapter 9, the
result is unfavorable even though additional deposits are identified under the stipulated design.
The correct product behavior is to retain the evidence and explain the cost of paying the
higher rate on balances that would have remained. It is not to search for a more favorable
estimator. A new targeted offer is a new policy requiring its own evaluation.
   For a sequential question, the same journey opens a trajectory view. The reader sees how
assistance affects next-month stress, eligibility and later costs. A latent-state model has an
additional observation and logging-law view: which signals measure the state, which variables
the historical actor used, and how that differs from the proposed actor. The fitted state is
presented as model-dependent uncertainty. This makes a POMDP estimation product useful
to a bank researcher before any automated action is authorized.


1.8     Why shared construction may be worth buying
The strongest integration benefit is the removal of repeated scientific translation. A team
today often reconstructs availability dates, rewrites entity-level folds, interprets a package’s
treatment coding and reassembles an evidence report for every study. The proposed library
6                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


would preserve those decisions in executable study objects, allowing a new estimator to be
a challenger for the same target. It would also make a source correction propagate to the
affected studies instead of silently changing a dashboard.
   That benefit is falsifiable. If every business unit needs a different outcome ontology, if
adapters consume as much work as a custom analysis, or if the evidence package cannot
shorten a real review, a shared product may have little advantage over a capable internal team
using open source. The economic comparison in Chapter 17 holds scientific quality and source
reconciliation obligations fixed. It counts shared costs once, measures the marginal application
cost and shows the portfolios for which reuse fails.
  The standalone buyer is consequently an institution with a portfolio of repeated causal
questions and a team able to own the assumptions. It is not a buyer seeking an automatic
answer to every causal question from raw data. The initial procurement can be a scientific
platform and supported analytical applications, with the bank retaining authoritative data
and model decisions. The same core can be installed as a library in the user’s repositories.
Both forms should produce the same estimand, score contributions and report on a shared
conformance fixture.


1.9    What this monograph constructs
The scientific chapters work from intervention definitions to estimators, dependence-aware
uncertainty, partially observed dynamics and graph search. The banking studies then use
those constructions in complete synthetic examples. They distinguish estimating balances
from valuing funding, evaluating a fixed policy from choosing one, and fitting a hidden-state
law from identifying a causal action. The data and software chapters explain what existing
tools supply and what a reusable platform must add.
   The numerical studies are deliberately transparent. Their assumptions, financial units,
training information and exact or model-based comparison values are visible. They establish
that the stated calculations can be constructed and expose several failure modes. They do
not estimate any named bank’s business opportunity. The proposal’s next investment is to
test the same scientific and engineering contracts on owned bank data, with equivalent-task
comparisons against existing practice.
Chapter 2

Identification before estimation

Identification determines whether a requested answer is a function of the available distribution
and stated assumptions. Estimation approximates that function from a finite sample. Com-
putation evaluates an estimator. The three questions fail in different ways: an observational
equivalence cannot be repaired by a larger cluster, a noisy identified effect may benefit from
more independent observations, and a slow valid estimator may benefit from better software.
A product must diagnose which problem it is facing.



2.1     The estimand is a product contract

For an eligible household let A ∈ {0, 1} denote assigned treatment, X information available
before assignment, and Y (a) the horizon outcome under assignment a. The average treatment
effect is
                  θ = E[Y (1) − Y (0)],     τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x].              (2.1)

The expectation refers to a declared population. An effect among existing high-balance
customers is not an effect among all households. Changing eligibility, outcome horizon or
economic valuation creates a new estimand. For offers, the intention-to-treat effect concerns
assignment; the effect of receipt requires a separate compliance design.
   Potential outcomes make the contrast explicit. Structural causal models describe how
interventions replace mechanisms. A single-world intervention graph links the two by splitting
a treatment node into its fixed intervention value and its random component (Hernán and
Robins, 2020; Peters et al., 2017; Richardson and Robins, 2013). The product should store
the estimand and, where used, a graph with substantive variable definitions. Neither notation
substitutes for a plausible assignment mechanism.
  Under consistency, conditional exchangeability {Y (0), Y (1)} ⊥ A | X, and positivity
0 < e(X) = P(A = 1 | X) < 1 on the target population,

                 θ = E[m1 (X) − m0 (X)],       ma (x) = E[Y | A = a, X = x].               (2.2)

Consistency includes the absence of consequential undisclosed treatment versions. An offer
is inadequately defined if its price, delivery and duration are unspecified. Exchangeability
concerns actual decision information: a relationship manager’s unrecorded knowledge can
invalidate it even if the warehouse contains thousands of predictive fields. Positivity concerns
actions within histories; large row counts do not create support for actions never taken.

                                               7
8                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


2.2     Experiments and observational studies
Randomize at household level when accounts share money, or at branch/region level when
capacity or communications spill across customers. Preserve actual allocation probabilities and
distinguish assignment, delivery and take-up. Experiments also need a prespecified horizon,
contamination diagnostics and attrition analysis.
   Adaptive experiments require their time-varying assignment probabilities and inference valid
for the adaptation and stopping rule. Repeatedly examining ordinary fixed-sample confidence
intervals does not make them valid under optional stopping. In a cluster experiment, the
number of randomized clusters constrains inference even with millions of transactions per
cluster. Randomization inference uses the actual allocation mechanism, not an analyst’s
preferred regression model.
   Observational adjustment is appropriate when assignment information and overlap are
defensible. Diagnostics include balance, propensity support, outcome sensitivity and negative
controls with justified causal roles. They can discover defects but do not prove that all
confounders were observed. The uncertainty object should distinguish sampling uncertainty
from assumptions about omitted confounding (Chernozhukov et al., 2022a).


2.3     Why orthogonal estimation is useful
Flexible prediction helps estimate nuisance functions ma and e, but direct substitution can
introduce regularization bias. An augmented inverse-probability score is

                                             A{Y − m1 (X)} (1 − A){Y − m0 (X)}
          ϕ(O; m, e) = m1 (X) − m0 (X) +                  −                    .              (2.3)
                                                 e(X)            1 − e(X)

Estimate nuisances outside the evaluation fold and average held-out scores. Cross-fitting
limits direct dependence between nuisance overfitting and evaluation residuals. Orthogonality
reduces first-order sensitivity to nuisance error (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Wager, 2025).

Proposition 2.1 (Conditional bias of the AIPW score). With true nuisances e, m0 , m1 , fixed
candidate nuisances ee, m

Proof. Conditioning on X replaces the treated residual term by e(m1 − m  e 1 )/ee and the untreated
residual term by −(1 − e)(m0 − m0 )/(1 − e). Collecting coefficients of each outcome error gives
                               e         e
the expression.

   The bias vanishes if either nuisance component is correct; otherwise it depends on products
of errors. With overlap bounds, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds these terms by products of nuisance-
error norms. Under the remaining independent-sampling and moment conditions, products
op (n−1/2 ) support asymptotically linear inference. This is not a result for arbitrarily dependent
transaction rows.
  For independent observations, the empirical held-out score variance divided by n estimates
the variance of the mean under suitable conditions. Household trajectories and common shocks
require appropriate score construction and covariance aggregation. The interface therefore
requires both an estimator and an inference specification.
2.4. A campaign example with a known answer                                                      9


2.4     A campaign example with a known answer

The synthetic construction sets X ∼ Bernoulli(1/2), e(X) = 0.2 + 0.6X, and

                    Y = 100 + 80X + (10 − 4X)A + ε,           ε ∼ N (0, 202 ).

The true effect is 8. In the population, P(X = 1 | A = 1) = 0.8 and P(X = 1 | A = 0) = 0.2.
The observed difference is 80(0.8 − 0.2) + 10 − 4(0.8) = 54.8: assignment targets customers
with larger untreated outcomes.
   In 40,000 independent synthetic households, five-fold saturated nuisance fits give AIPW
8.472 with standard error 0.254, compared with the raw difference 55.586. The 95% interval is
approximately [7.974, 8.969]. This checks a computation against a known process. One seed
and an interval containing the truth do not demonstrate coverage.
   Heterogeneity matters economically. Effects are 10 and 6 in the two groups. At an additional
cost of 7 per offer, treating everyone has true incremental value 1 per eligible customer; treating
only X = 0 has value 1.5. The code evaluates these fixed policies with paired AIPW scores and
simultaneous intervals over three declared comparisons. This demonstrates policy comparison
without optimizing and evaluating a learned policy on the same outcomes. The targeted-versus-
all estimate is 0.336 with a simultaneous interval approximately [−0.096, 0.769]. Although
the generating model makes the targeted policy better by 0.5, this sample does not establish
superiority at the declared simultaneous confidence level. Both policies have positive lower
bounds relative to treating nobody. The example thus distinguishes positive value from
evidence that a more selective policy is better.



2.5     Heterogeneity, instruments and thresholds

Meta-learners and orthogonal learners estimate conditional average effects (Künzel et al., 2019;
Chernozhukov et al., 2018). Compare subgroup calibration, policy value and uncertainty, not
only factual prediction. Suppress unsupported segments. A customer’s CATE is an average
among comparable customers, not an observable personal causal effect.
   When assignment has unmeasured determinants, a valid instrument can offer a different
route (Chernozhukov et al., 2024). With binary randomized encouragement Z, exclusion,
relevance, independence and monotone take-up identify the complier effect through the Wald
ratio
                                   E[Y | Z = 1] − E[Y | Z = 0]
                          θLATE =                              .                      (2.5)
                                   E[A | Z = 1] − E[A | Z = 0]

Monotonicity and exclusion are not consequences of a strong first stage. Weak first stages need
suitable inference. Competitor rates may directly affect switching and therefore fail exclusion.
A price instrument valid in one market can fail in another because information and policy
differ.
   Regression discontinuity uses a treatment rule at a threshold c of a running variable R.
With continuity of potential-outcome means, the outcome jump identifies a local effect in a
sharp design. In a fuzzy design divide the outcome jump by the treatment-probability jump,
with appropriate compliance restrictions. Retain the score and rule version used at the time;
inspect manipulation, competing thresholds and bandwidth sensitivity. The local effect does
not by itself value a policy far from the threshold.
10                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


2.6     What a result is allowed to say
Every result identifies its design, target, comparison, assumptions and uncertainty. Its scientific
state may be identified under declared assumptions, partially identified, unsupported by observed
action overlap, or not identified under the supplied model. Numerical convergence is a separate
field. A consuming application can then abstain or request a better experiment without
mistaking prediction for identification.


2.7     Why the augmented score works
The AIPW score has a useful interpretation for a banker. It first predicts each customer’s
outcome under each action, then corrects the prediction using the observed residual among
customers who actually received that action. A rare action receives a larger correction because
fewer observed customers represent its potential outcome. The estimator does not create
counterfactual observations; it uses exchangeability to give those residuals their intervention
interpretation.
   Equation (2.4) makes that forecast-and-correction account precise. Conditioning on training
information treats fitted functions as fixed for an independent evaluation observation; averaging
the conditional remainder gives the population bias. The relevant protection concerns the
product of nuisance errors, with the overlap and inference conditions already stated. It does
not assert that two inaccurate learners necessarily cancel.
   For bank data, overlap can vary sharply by product, jurisdiction and eligibility rule. A risk
department may never approve a limit increase for a certain population. No flexible outcome
learner makes the intervention identified there from those records. Trimming changes the
population; capping weights changes the estimator’s bias; replacing a deterministic policy by a
feasible stochastic policy changes the estimand. Each can be reasonable, but the report must
describe the actual choice and recompute the economic target accordingly.


2.8     Residualization can change the target
Partially linear DML is attractive because it combines flexible nuisance prediction with a
low-dimensional coefficient. Its canonical model is

        Y = θ0 A + g0 (X) + U,    E[U | A, X] = 0,       A = e0 (X) + V,    E[V | X] = 0.

Let ℓ0 (X) = E[Y | X]. Regress the residualized outcome Y − ℓ0 (X) on A − e0 (X), or solve
the orthogonal moment

                       E[(A − e0 (X)){Y − ℓ0 (X) − θ(A − e0 (X))}] = 0.                       (2.6)

Cross-fitting allows flexible estimates of e0 and ℓ0 while retaining a tractable target under the
model and rate assumptions.
  Now suppose the true effect is τ (X) rather than a constant. For a binary action with
conditional mean m0 (X) + Aτ (X), the population solution of the same moment is
                                       E[e0 (X){1 − e0 (X)}τ (X)]
                              θPLR =                              .                           (2.7)
                                         E[e0 (X){1 − e0 (X)}]
To obtain it, condition the numerator E[(A − e0 )(Y − ℓ0 )] on X; it equals the conditional
treatment variance times τ (X). The denominator averages that same variance. The resulting
2.9. Selecting covariates requires temporal and causal reasoning                                 11


coefficient emphasizes customers with treatment probabilities near one half. It need not equal
the eligible population’s ATE or an effect among treated customers.
   This distinction is operational. A bank could compare an AIPW ATE to a partially linear
DML coefficient, see different values and incorrectly attribute the difference to software quality.
The estimates may target different weighted populations. A challenger comparison must
either align the target or state the different question. The adapter registry therefore needs an
estimand declaration, including aggregation weights, rather than only a label such as “DML
supported.”


2.9     Selecting covariates requires temporal and causal reasoning

A variable measured before an action can still be inappropriate to adjust for if it is a collider or
an instrument that aggravates variance without addressing confounding. A variable measured
after an action can be a mediator, a common effect or a confounder of a later decision. The
temporal clock is necessary, but it does not decide every adjustment question.
   For example, an offer A0 changes engagement L1 , which affects both future assistance A1
and final recoveries Y . Adjusting for L1 in a single regression intended to estimate the total
A0 effect can block part of that effect. Failing to adjust for it when evaluating A1 can leave
confounding. Chapter 4 resolves this through the sequential law. It cannot be resolved by a
global “pre-treatment features” list shared by all decision dates.
   The same issue appears in customer service data. Complaints can result from both an
offer and latent dissatisfaction. Conditioning on complaint receipt may select a subgroup
whose latent dissatisfaction differs across offers. An analysis of customers with a recorded
complaint then targets neither the original cohort nor an automatically valid mediator effect.
A mediation study needs its own intervention definition and identifying assumptions; the total
assignment effect remains useful even when the mechanism is unresolved (Hernán and Robins,
2020; Richardson and Robins, 2013).
   The proposed data organizer can suggest which columns describe complaints, assignments
and account outcomes. It can identify timestamps and draw candidate graphs. It cannot infer
that a complaint is an acceptable adjustment variable from its business name. The study must
retain the reason it is included, excluded or treated as a time-varying variable.


2.10      Measurement, missingness and transport are part of iden-
          tification

Suppose true treatment is an assigned offer but the source records only an opened message.
The measurement is then affected by attention, device use and customer preference. Relabeling
message opening as treatment changes the intervention. Recovering a hidden treatment from
surrogates requires additional measurement and proxy restrictions; recent work does not justify
universal recovery of missing action logs (Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2026).
   Likewise, a missing competitor balance is not a zero balance. If observed bank balance
equals liquid wealth times bank share, B = W ω, the same B is compatible with many (W, ω)
pairs. Neither precise measurement of B nor a flexible causal learner identifies the outside
wallet without additional information. Data-recovery draws can propagate uncertainty under
a supplied missingness model, but they do not establish that model. The corrupted-data
literature makes clear that different measurement and observation operators require different
identification conditions (Agarwal and Singh, 2022).
12                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


   For a source population S = 1 and a target population S = 0, transporting an effect requires
more than matching feature names. If conditional causal effects are stable and every target X
has source support, the target ATE is E[τ (X) | S = 0]. This is a useful standardization formula.
It does not follow merely because a classifier has difficulty distinguishing the populations.
Product terms, laws, delivery systems, hidden effect modifiers and competitive responses may
change the response mechanism. The target population and stability assumptions must remain
attached to the transported estimate.


2.11     From an effect to a financial comparison
Let Ck (a) be dated cash or economic contribution components with signs defined from the
group’s perspective, and let dk be fixed discount and currency-conversion factors. Define
        P
Y (a) = k dk Ck (a). Linearity gives
                                               X
                          E[Y (1) − Y (0)] =       dk E[Ck (1) − Ck (0)].
                                               k

However, uncertainty is joint. If θb estimates the component effects with covariance Σ, b the
variance of the financial contrast is d′ Σd.
                                         b   Adding component confidence intervals or treating
correlated components as independent does not reproduce this variance. Fitting all components
on the same folds and retaining customer or cluster score vectors allows the covariance to be
reconstructed.
   This formula conditions on fixed financial factors. An uncertain transfer price, loss severity
or capital charge adds parameter and scenario uncertainty. If the policy changes aggregate
market rates, the factors can themselves be intervention-dependent. Then a common fixed
conversion is an approximation whose adequacy needs an economic argument. Deposit principal
is a funding quantity; its full value is not an immediate profit. Similarly, a loan advance is
an outflow paired with a claim, not an expense that should be counted again when expected
principal losses are recorded.
   Scientific uncertainty and economic sensitivity should be displayed separately and, where a
defensible joint model exists, combined. A narrow sampling interval under one accounting
convention does not settle a decision that reverses under plausible funding-cost or customer-
response assumptions.
Chapter 3

Panels, policy changes and banking
economics

3.1     Repeated measurement is not a design
Bank panels combine households, firms, accounts, branches and calendar dates. They separate
persistent differences from changes over time but do not automatically remove time-varying
confounding. In
                                 Yit = αi + λt + βDit + uit ,                         (3.1)
unit effects absorb time-constant additive heterogeneity and time effects absorb common
additive shocks. Neither absorbs a local recession affecting both rollout and outcomes. The
coefficient must match the economic target. Modern designs include group-time effects,
imputation, synthetic controls and interactive factors (Arkhangelsky and Imbens, 2024; Roth
et al., 2023).

3.1.1    What the within transformation actually removes

For a balanced panel define Zeit = Zit − Z̄i· − Z̄·t + Z̄·· . Applying this linear operation to
Equation (3.1) removes both additive effects. A scalar coefficient is estimated by
                                                 P
                                                  it Dit Yit
                                                      e e
                                          βb =               .                                   (3.2)
                                                 P     e2
                                                    it Dit

The denominator shows the source of information: treatment variation left after unit and date
effects. A national policy adopted by every bank at the same time has no such variation in this
specification. Millions of accounts cannot rescue that rank failure. For an unbalanced panel,
successive simple demeaning does not generally equal the exact joint projection; a suitable
least-squares or converged absorption routine is needed.
   A sufficient model-based condition for the usual within moment is strict exogeneity, E[uit |
Di1 , . . . , DiT , αi ] = 0, together with the appropriate common-effect specification. This excludes
feedback from an unobserved outcome shock into later treatment. Bank managers often change
offers after unexpected withdrawals, so the condition can fail even if today’s treatment predates
today’s recorded outcome. Predeterminedness is weaker and does not in general justify the
same within estimator. The policy-study route should therefore start with its design, not infer
exogeneity from a familiar regression formula.
  The transformation also cannot remove an arbitrary function of latent heterogeneity. If
untreated deposits are Yit (0) = exp(αi + ft ) + ϵit , subtracting unit and date means leaves

                                                 13
14                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


interactions between the customer and the macro state. A machine learner fitted to demeaned
data inherits that problem. The panel DML discussion in Fuhr and Papies (2024) is relevant
precisely because nonlinear latent heterogeneity and dependence complicate otherwise useful
orthogonal-learning constructions.


3.2     Staggered adoption and explicit aggregation
Let Gi be the first treatment date, with Gi = ∞ for never-treated entities. An absorbing
rollout defines
                     ATT(g, t) = E[Yit (g) − Yit (∞) | Gi = g], t ≥ g.
With no anticipation and conditional parallel trends between cohort g and valid controls C,
                                     
                        ATT(g, t) = E E[Yt − Yg−1 | G = g, X]
                                                                           
                                         − E[Yt − Yg−1 | C = 1, X] | G = g .                   (3.3)

Controls remain untreated over the comparison interval and have support for the treated
cohort. The outer expectation targets the treated covariate distribution. Never-treated and
not-yet-treated comparison groups imply different assumptions and available dates (Callaway
and Sant’Anna, 2021).
                                              P
  Aggregation is part of the estimand: θ = g,t wgt ATT(g, t) for declared nonnegative weights
summing to one. Equal customer, branch and treated-period weights answer different questions.
Event-time effects also change cohort composition when long follow-up is available only for
early adopters.
   Goodman-Bacon (2021) decompose TWFE into two-by-two comparisons. Sun and Abraham
(2021) show that lead/lag coefficients can mix effects across event times. Borusyak et al. (2024)
make target weights and the untreated outcome model explicit through imputation. The
product should expose these alternatives rather than label every fixed-effects regression valid
DiD.

Example 3.1 (Perfect untreated trends, misleading TWFE). Three equal cohorts are observed
over four dates. The early cohort adopts at date 2 with effects (1, 4, 8); the late cohort adopts
at date 4 with effect 1; the third never adopts. Untreated outcomes equal a cohort intercept
plus a common linear trend. The four-treated-cell average is (1 + 4 + 8 + 1)/4 = 3.5.
   Residualizing treatment on cohort and time effects yields underlying effect weights
(0.3, 0.3, −0.1, 0.5). Thus TWFE is 0.3 + 1.2 − 0.8 + 0.5 = 1.2. Comparisons with the
never-treated cohort recover every group-time effect and their average 3.5.

   This is a target and comparison problem; clustering standard errors does not repair it. A
rollout with gradually growing adoption can exhibit this pattern.


3.2.1    A doubly robust cohort comparison

For one cohort and comparison interval, retain only cohort g and controls that are untreated
over the interval. Let D = 1 indicate cohort g, ∆Y = Yt − Yg−1 , p(X) = P(D = 1 | X), and
m0 (X) = E[∆Y | D = 0, X] in this restricted population. Write q = P(D = 1). A population
score for the cohort ATT is

Figure 3.1: Exact synthetic panel calculation. Contamination occurs despite correct untreated
parallel trends.


Under no anticipation, overlap and conditional parallel trends, the first term compares treated
changes with their counterfactual untreated change. The second corrects a fitted untreated-
change regression using reweighted control residuals. Its weights map control covariates to
the treated distribution. With either the relevant propensity or untreated-change regression
correct, the mean has the desired robustness; a sample version also estimates the cohort share
and carries its uncertainty. This is a simple form of the identification and estimation logic
developed by Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021).
   Notice what differs from a static treatment-effect model. The identifying assumption
concerns untreated changes, not the levels of untreated outcomes. A treated branch can
have a permanently different customer mix and deposit level. It becomes a problem when its
untreated change would differ after the rollout, conditional on the stated covariates. Including
post-rollout customer composition as a control can itself remove a policy mechanism, since the
rollout may attract a different customer population.
   The common score representation is useful for software. Once each ATT(g, t) has cluster
contributions, an aggregate effect uses the same declared weights on those contributions. A
covariance matrix over event times then supports simultaneous bands and financial aggregation.
Repeatedly calling a package for separate dates and discarding cross-date covariance loses
information required to value a multi-month policy.



3.2.2                          The comparison set is an economic choice

Never-treated branches may be structurally unlike rollout branches. Not-yet-treated branches
can be more comparable but can anticipate a scheduled change. A one-month anticipation
allowance changes the last valid baseline and excludes controls close to their own adoption.
When every branch eventually adopts, late effects may have no untreated controls. The honest
output is then a shorter identified horizon or a more model- dependent extrapolation, rather
than a graph with silently declining support.
   Event-time aggregation needs a second decision. At event month 12 only early cohorts may
remain observable. Comparing that average with event month 1 can conflate effect dynamics
with a different cohort mix. A balanced event window estimates the same cohorts at every
horizon but discards information. The report should show both the target weights and the
set of contributing cohorts. A bank sponsor can then decide whether the retained target
population matches the planned rollout.
16                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


3.3     Trend sensitivity and reversals
An insignificant pretrend test does not establish parallel trends. Low power and post-selection
affect interpretation. Rambachan and Roth (2023) allow specified smoothness or relative-
magnitude deviations. Show conclusions over a justified sensitivity range and the point at
which the decision changes.

3.3.1    Sensitivity gives the assumption an economic scale

Suppose a simple two-period estimate is τb. Let δ be the treated-minus-control change in
untreated potential outcomes, so that E[τb] = τ + δ under the rest of the design. If substantive
reasoning limits δ to [−M, M ], the compatible treatment effects shift by that range. An
approximate sampling interval [L, U ] becomes a conservative union [L − M, U + M ] when that
bound is treated as fixed. This elementary construction is deliberately separate from the more
structured event-study confidence sets in Rambachan and Roth (2023).
   The parameter should be expressed in business units. If a positive policy decision reverses
when untreated deposits could have grown only USD 20 per eligible customer more rapidly in
treated branches, that is useful information for a funding economist. A sensitivity parameter
whose relation to deposit growth is hidden behind a default slider is less useful. Historical
untreated variation, known local shocks and institutional rollout rules can motivate a range,
but do not prove its bound.
   Pre-treatment coefficients have two roles: they can reveal contradictions with a design,
and they can help calibrate a sensitivity analysis. Passing a pretrend test is not a license to
assume M = 0. Selection of the final design after searching for quiet pretrends can distort the
subsequent interval. The product records the original study plan and exploratory alternatives
so that the final inference can be interpreted honestly.
   Bank treatments also change intensity or reverse: rates move repeatedly, contact policies
stop and restart, and branch services expand in stages. Absorbing binary-adoption methods
may be inappropriate. de Chaisemartin and D’Haultfœuille (2024), in the archived May 2026
revision, study intertemporal effects with status-quo comparisons for groups sharing initial
treatment. No anticipation, comparison support and treatment-path meaning remain essential.
Preserve intensity and version rather than collapsing every history to first treatment.


3.4     Dynamic panels and latent factors
In
                                Yit = ρYi,t−1 + βAit + αi + εit ,
demeaning correlates the transformed lagged outcome and disturbance in a short panel.
Differencing removes αi but not endogeneity. Under suitable serial-correlation and initial-
condition restrictions, lagged levels instrument differenced equations. Moments such as
E[Yi,t−s ∆εit ] = 0, s ≥ 2, require justification. Arellano and Bond (1991) develop relevant
specification tests. First-order correlation in differenced errors may be mechanical; higher-order
tests, instrument validity and sensitivity to instrument count matter.

3.4.1    Deriving an internal-instrument moment

First differencing the dynamic model gives
                               ∆Yit = ρ∆Yi,t−1 + β∆Ait + ∆εit .
3.5. Synthetic controls and structural time series                                                17


The regressor ∆Yi,t−1 contains εi,t−1 , whereas the disturbance contains −εi,t−1 . Even indepen-
dent level errors therefore create a correlation. Under serially uncorrelated level innovations
and suitable initial conditions, Yi,t−2 is orthogonal to both εit and εi,t−1 . It can instrument
∆Yi,t−1 . Older levels provide additional moments, but the allowable lags for A depend on
whether actions are strictly exogenous, predetermined or contemporaneously endogenous.
   Stack admissible instruments in Zi and differenced residuals in vi (ϑ). The sample moment
is ḡ(ϑ) = N −1 i Zi′ vi (ϑ), and GMM minimizes ḡ(ϑ)′ W ḡ(ϑ) for a suitable weighting matrix.
               P

Robust covariance estimation uses unit-level moment contributions; the two-step weighting
matrix and its finite-sample behavior need explicit treatment. This construction explains why
dynamic panel software requires the instrument set, transformation and inference convention
to be part of the saved model (Arellano and Bond, 1991).
  Persistence creates another problem. If levels are highly persistent, lagged levels may be
weak instruments for changes. Enlarging the instrument set can overfit endogenous changes
and make overidentification diagnostics unhelpful. A sensible comparison limits lag depth,
considers collapsed instrument sets and reports sensitivity; it does not select the specification
with the most reassuring diagnostic p-value. A system of additional level-equation moments
needs additional stationarity or initial-condition restrictions. It is a different identifying model,
not an automatic upgrade whenever difference GMM is imprecise.
  Interactive-factor models Yit (0) = αi + λt + ℓ⊤
                                                 i ft + εit permit different exposures to common
shocks. Factor rank, untreated-data availability, treatment selection and extrapolation govern
their use. An estimated factor is not automatically a measured confounder.
  Panel DML combines flexible nuisances with panel structure, but nonlinear latent hetero-
geneity need not disappear under a within transformation. Fuhr and Papies (2024) examine
point estimation in simulation. Chiang et al. (2021) establish multiway-cluster DML results
under specified exchangeability and dissociation conditions. These are not guarantees for
arbitrary serial dependence.


3.5     Synthetic controls and structural time series
                                                              P
For a small number of policy changes, construct Yb1t (0) = j∈D wj Yjt from suitable untreated
donors, often with nonnegative weights summing to one. Pre-fit assesses one aspect of
plausibility; interpolation bias and spillovers remain concerns (Abadie et al., 2010; Abadie,
2021). Outcome-model augmentation can correct imperfect fit while implying negative weights
(Ben-Michael et al., 2021).
  Synthetic DiD combines unit and time weighting (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021). Its inspected
package documents block treatment: paper extensions do not prove implementation support.
Bayesian structural time-series methods offer another counterfactual forecast (Brodersen et al.,
2015). Controls must be unaffected and their counterfactual relationship must remain credible.
  Nearby branches receiving displaced customers after a closure may be invalid donors.
National campaign controls may share exposure. Placebo dates, donor sensitivity and pre-
period holdouts can challenge a design; they cannot create an untreated comparison where
none exists.


3.5.1    What a donor fit identifies

One useful model writes untreated outcomes as Yit (0) = αi + λt + ℓ′i ft + ϵit . If donor weights
reproduce the treated unit’s intercept and factor loading, their weighted untreated mean
reproduces its systematic counterfactual. A long and informative pre-period can constrain
18                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


those loadings through outcome fit. It does not ensure that a novel post-period factor lies in
the same span or that donor outcomes remain unaffected.
   The conventional nonnegative simplex constraint controls extrapolation: the synthetic unit
lies in the donors’ convex hull. If the treated unit is outside that hull, poor fit can persist
even with many donors. Augmentation uses an outcome model to correct residual imbalance
and can permit negative effective weights (Ben-Michael et al., 2021). It exchanges a stricter
interpolation restriction for a model-dependent extrapolation. Synthetic DiD balances both
units and dates in its main block-adoption setting (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021). These are
distinct responses to imperfect comparison data; neither is uniformly preferable.
   Inference must match the design. A placebo distribution across donors can be informative
when units are suitably exchangeable under the null and fit differences are handled. It is
not automatically a randomized test when a regulator deliberately selected one troubled
institution. Time-series posterior predictive intervals condition on the counterfactual model
and its unaffected controls (Brodersen et al., 2015). Their coverage is not a test of the causal
exclusion. A bank report should distinguish sampling, model and design uncertainty instead
of merging all three into one shaded band labeled “confidence.”


3.6     Financial interpretation and uncertainty
Independent policy changes constrain information more than raw account counts. Bertrand
et al. (2004) demonstrate the consequences of ignored serial correlation. Preserve assignment
clusters and disclose few-cluster or short-time limitations.
   The lending design of Mian and Khwaja (2006) compares bank supply among multi-bank
borrowers; it does not directly estimate all borrowers’ losses. The mortgage equilibrium
analysis of Benetton (2021) adds demand and supply assumptions. Regional effects in Beraja
et al. (2019) cannot simply be summed into an aggregate monetary-policy effect. Preserve the
distinction between an identified local effect, a transported effect and a structural scenario.

Repeated decisions, hidden states

Longitudinal interventions and

4.1     Why a sequence changes the problem
In collections, yesterday’s assistance affects today’s arrears, today’s arrears influence the next
assistance decision, and both predict eventual repayment. Today’s arrears are therefore both a
consequence of earlier treatment and a confounder for later treatment. Regressing repayment
on every action and every intermediate covariate can remove part of the total effect of earlier
assistance. Omitting the covariate can confound the later effect.
   Let Lt be information available immediately before decision At , Ht = (L0 , A0 , . . . , At−1 , Lt ),
and let decisions occur at t = 0, . . . , T −1. A policy gt (a | h) specifies a distribution over feasible
actions at each history. A deterministic rule is the special case concentrated at a = dt (h). The
target is
                           ψ(g) = E[Y g ],        ∆(g, g0 ) = ψ(g) − ψ(g0 ),                         (4.1)
with population, horizon, outcome and eligibility stated. A comparison of one action at baseline
differs from a comparison of sustained strategies.

                                          −1

At true nuisance functions, each weighted residual has mean zero by iterated expectation.
Cross-fitted recursive estimators use this structure to limit nuisance bias. Nested-function and
longitudinal-rate analyses explain the needed products of nuisance errors (Chernozhukov et al.,
2022b; Singh, 2022). Sequential double robustness can hold when an appropriate outcome or
treatment component is correct at each stage (Luedtke et al., 2018); this property requires the
corresponding recursive construction and cannot be assigned to every algorithm labeled DR.
   Longitudinal targeted estimation updates an initial outcome regression along a fluctuation
informed by treatment/censoring weights, aiming to solve the influence-function estimating
equation while respecting outcome bounds. It is a useful alternative to a one-step estimator,
especially for bounded risks. The target, nuisance fits, targeting convergence and support
diagnostics must all be retained. A point estimate from a neural sequence predictor does not
supply these inferential properties.
   Dynamic DML via g-estimation uses orthogonal residualization and recursive removal of
future effects in a structured dynamic model (Lewis and Syrgkanis, 2021). Its independent-
trajectory formulation suits some many-customer panels. It does not directly supply a theorem
for one unrestricted aggregate bank series. The product must expose the chosen effect
parameterization, not relabel all dynamic models a single method.

Set L0 ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) and

                           P(A0 = 1 | L0 ) = 0.2 + 0.6L0 ,
                        P(L1 = 1 | L0 , A0 ) = 0.1 + 0.5L0 + 0.2A0 ,
                    P(A1 = 1 | L0 , A0 , L1 ) = 0.15 + 0.5L1 + 0.1A0 ,
                                            Y = 20 + 3A0 + 4A1 + 10L1 + 6L0 .

Every relevant action has positive probability. Under always versus never treat, direct
contributions add 3 + 4 = 7 and the mediated change in L1 adds 10(0.2) = 2. The total is 9.
The intervention means are 35.5 and 26.5.
   Enumerating all 16 observed cells verifies that the g-formula and exact IPW reproduce both
means. The observed always-adherer versus never-adherer contrast is 19.137. A correctly
specified conditional outcome regression includes L1 but its two action coefficients sum only to
7; that sum excludes the mediated component. The lesson concerns the causal contrast, not
an inability of regression to fit the observed outcome.

4.5                                              Feasible interventions and weak support
An always-assist policy may be unsupported for low-risk customers or ineligible accounts.
Incremental interventions instead multiply treatment odds by δ > 0:
                                                                                                   δet (1 | h)
                                                                         gδ,t (1 | h) =                                .                                                  (4.7)
                                                                                          δet (1 | h) + 1 − et (1 | h)
These preserve deterministic zero/one assignment regions (Kennedy, 2019). They answer how
outcomes change under an odds shift, not under universal treatment. Since the target itself
depends on the observed propensity law, its efficient score is not obtained by blindly treating
gδ as externally fixed in Equation (4.6).
   Modified treatment policies can shift a rate or limit while respecting conditional support
(Díaz et al., 2023). A natural-value modification and its stochastic analogue may require
different sequential randomization conditions. An economically feasible shift also needs a clear
operational implementation: a mathematical intervention on utilization is not necessarily an
action the bank can directly perform.


4.6                                              Censoring, eligibility and competing events
Account closure, debt sale, default, prepayment and loss of observation have different mean-
ings. If an outcome remains well-defined but becomes unobserved, identification can require
conditional independent censoring and positive observation probability. Artificial censoring at
deviation from a treatment regime introduces an additional weighting or modeling task. If
treatment changes eligibility for a later action, simply restricting to observed survivors changes
the target population.
4.7. Deep sequence models and the product boundary                                                             23


   Jiang et al. (2025) explicitly model treatment-dependent eligibility; their monotone eligibility
setup must be checked against banking re-entry and repeat episodes. Shah et al. (2026) derive
dynamic-regime cumulative incidence methods with competing risks in a recent preprint. These
motivate separate outcome contracts for default and prepayment.
  For disjoint terminal events with regime-specific marginal hazards λgD,k and λgP,k among

Estimating these regime hazards still requires longitudinal identification. Censoring prepayment
and calling the result the actual probability of default would answer a different, potentially
hypothetical question. A customer-value outcome can incorporate both terminal events directly,
provided cash-flow ownership and observation are defined.


4.7     Deep sequence models and the product boundary
Counterfactual recurrent networks, causal transformers and neural g-computation supply
flexible representations or transition estimators (Bica et al., 2020; Melnychuk et al., 2022;
Li et al., 2020). The inspected texts retain consistency, sequential ignorability and overlap.
Attention or adversarial balance does not verify those assumptions.
   They are appropriate challengers when long histories and nonlinear dynamics defeat simpler
models. Evaluate simulated interventions, misspecification, support and policy value alongside
factual prediction. Use simpler g-computation, IPW and recursive DR comparators with the
same target. The first product should support a modest set of interpretable policies and
explicit horizons before claiming arbitrary long-horizon optimization.

Proof. With correct ratios, each weighted dated quantity has its expectation under the

ratio leaves its mean zero.

are concentrated.
