  SMEwallet’s model card limits completed evidence to a synthetic prototype and reports
no promoted learned policy. Its scenarios are useful adverse cases, not competitor-wallet
ground truth. The inspected MacroFinance milestone note discusses covariance provenance
and conditional identification; it is an earlier document, not a current overall status assessment.
  For cardnpv, an adapter must map explicitly from any internal treatment-minus-comparator
convention to its canonical historical-minus- perfect-execution direction. Test the sign on a
known two-value fixture. A numerically accurate sign reversal is a material financial error.
  Integration begins with schema validation, then a synthetic adapter, independent reference
agreement and bank qualification. Repositories can adopt contracts independently. Version
mismatch must fail visibly rather than discard fields.


14.5       Deployment and operations
Offer deployment inside the bank’s controlled cloud or premises, plus local research mode. A
control service manages metadata, authorization and jobs; workers run near data. Sensitive
rows do not belong in application logs, source-control repositories or paper-research artifacts.
   Use enterprise identity, least-privilege access, encryption, audited artifacts, retention policies
and secrets management. These are proposed requirements, to be validated in integration and
security tests. Legal-entity and regional separation applies to caches, features, models and
exports as well as source tables.
   Pin adapter environments and software bills of materials. Retain exact versions, licenses,
vulnerability-review results and seeds for qualified releases. Upgrade through reference, adverse-
case and contract tests: changed treatment coding, covariance defaults or graph endpoints can
alter a scientific conclusion.
14.6. Model governance and current guidance                                                   85


  Monitor data freshness, missingness, support, outcome delay, policy version, graph stability
and effect drift. Alarms should trigger recomputation, restricted use or a redesigned study.
They must not silently relax identification assumptions.


14.6     Model governance and current guidance
Federal Reserve SR26-2 distributes April 2026 interagency guidance that supersedes SR11-7
and SR21-8. It emphasizes risk-based governance, conceptual soundness, outcomes analysis,
effective challenge and vendor responsibility (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
and other federal banking agencies, 2026). Its supervisory applicability is specific; it is not a
global bank rule. The scope footnote excludes generative and agentic AI models while covering
traditional quantitative and non-generative, non-agentic AI. The semantic-assistance layer
therefore needs the bank’s applicable governance assessment rather than an assertion that the
guidance directly covers every component.
   PRA SS1/23 was revised in April 2026. It covers specified UK-incorporated firms with
internal-model regulatory-capital permission, with exclusions stated in the document (Bank
of England Prudential Regulation Authority, 2026). Its principles address model lifecycle
and self-assessment. Map each legal entity and use to applicable requirements. The product
supplies evidence; it cannot confer approval.
Chapter 15

Construction specification and
measured components

15.1     An operation must preserve the study’s meaning
The implementation should make the scientific argument reproducible across execution environ-
ments. A scientist who requests an average effect on the original eligible cohort should receive
that target whether the job runs in a notebook, a service worker or a distributed warehouse.
Removing closed accounts, changing fold boundaries or averaging branch coefficients with
different weights changes the analysis even if every local function succeeds. The unit of
composition is therefore a versioned study and its artifacts.
   The proposal supplies two small working components: historical event reconstruction and
crossed-cluster score reduction. It also supplies fitted research studies and four JSON contracts.
These establish selected semantics and calculations. The general study compiler, service
endpoints, user workspaces, distributed scheduler and sibling adapters described here remain
proposed construction. Keeping that boundary explicit lets an implementation team identify
its actual starting point.


15.2     Package boundaries and owned invariants
The proposed packages divide responsibility by the invariant they preserve. The data package
owns historical identity, observation status, availability and reconciled economic components.
The design package owns the estimand, intervention versions, identification route, assumptions
and target weights. The execution package owns folds, model dependencies, resource limits
and retry semantics. Estimation adapters own the translation to an explicitly supported
external method. The inference package owns score meaning, dependence, resampling and
simultaneous contrasts. The evidence package owns immutable reconstruction, source identity
and permission-aware exports.
   These packages should exchange documented arrays and records rather than opaque frame-
work objects. A trajectory artifact records trajectory key, calendar key, decision index, action
and eligibility mask, pre-action information, outcomes, censoring and model-training role. An
irregular history cannot be padded into a balanced panel without recording which positions
are structural absence, unobserved visits or actual zeros. An adapter requiring equal-length
histories must reject or explicitly transform an incompatible artifact.



                                               86
15.3. The implemented temporal reference                                                           87


  Operation             Required input                     Returned artifact or refusal
  Reconstruct           Decision episodes, event           Selected revisions, features,
  snapshot              revisions, entity and coverage     observation masks, reconciliation
                        rules
  Compile design        Study, snapshot, graph               Estimand and identification
                        assumptions, target population       status, fold plan, supported
                                                             methods
  Fit                   Training partition,                  Model, training lineage,
  nuisance/model        method/version, seed, resource convergence and support
                        limit                                diagnostics
  Evaluate scores       Frozen models, evaluation            Defined score vector, cluster keys,
                        partition, policy/target weights extreme-contribution diagnostics
  Infer contrasts       Complete score partitions,           Point estimate, labeled
                        covariance specification             uncertainty, covariance and
                                                             limitations
  Export evidence       Completed run and authorized Reconstruction manifest, scientific
                        artifact references                  report and financial account
                Table 15.1: Proposed operation contracts. Each refusal identi-
                fies a specific missing condition; it is not a request to silently
                choose a new target.



   A model fit can finish while its transition parameters remain weakly determined. A design can
be valid while a particular fitted model reaches its iteration cap. A job can be canceled before
a complete covariance is available. The result should therefore carry separate computational,
scientific and evidence states. Suggested computational states are queued, running, complete,
failed and canceled. Scientific states distinguish identified under declared assumptions, partially
identified, conditional scenario and unresolved. Evidence states distinguish exact construction,
synthetic study, retrospective bank study and prospective evaluation. One green success flag
cannot communicate all three.


15.3      The implemented temporal reference
The small Python package is named causalbank-research, version 0.2.0. Its Event and
Decision records and compile_snapshot function implement the revision ordering in Chap-
ter 12. For example:
from causalbank import Event, Decision, compile_snapshot

events = [
    Event("credit", "H1", "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z",
         "2026-01-03T00:00:00Z", 1, 100.0, "USD"),
    Event("credit", "H1", "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z",
         "2026-01-10T00:00:00Z", 2, 60.0, "USD"),
]
decisions = [Decision("d1", "H1", "2026-01-08T00:00:00Z")]
snapshot = compile_snapshot(
    events, decisions, lookback_days=30,
    currency="USD", feed_complete=True)
assert snapshot["rows"][0]["amount"] == 100.0
88                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


The result lists the selected event revision and a hash of the declared input account. Reversing
input event order preserves the result. A duplicate event revision, changed event owner,
nonfinite amount, incompatible currency or timestamp without a timezone produces an error.
The feed-completeness declaration is required before absence becomes an additive zero.
   This reference deliberately uses an inspectable per-decision algorithm. It is not the imple-
mentation to scan a banking group’s full transaction history. A warehouse adapter should
implement the same semantics with indexed intervals, partition pruning and revision-aware
joins, then pass the same independent account fixture. Hashing a complete local input collec-
tion also differs from production content addressing: a large job should use immutable dataset
manifests and partition digests instead of rereading every byte at each operation.
   Availability at exactly the recorded decision instant is treated as known in the reference.
A real decision system may require a strict predecessor rule or a publication-latency margin.
The source sequence number and the decision system’s clock precision determine that choice.
It must be a versioned convention; changing it creates a new snapshot.


15.4     The implemented score reducer
Let xj ∈ Rd be an already computed, equally weighted score vector. Write n for its row
count, x̄ = n−1 j xj , and Sg = j∈g xj , ng = |g| for a declared cluster. The centered cluster
                 P               P

contribution is Ug = Sg − ng x̄. For G nonempty clusters, the component covariance used by
the reference is
                                          G 1 X
                                   VbG =             Ug Ug′ .
                                         G − 1 n2 g

Entity, date and entity–date intersections give Vb = VbE + VbT − VbET . Retaining intersection
groups matters when multiple scores occupy the same entity/date cell. Replacing the last term
by an ordinary row covariance would then generally compute a different quantity.
   Raw counts and sums are additive across partitions. The reducer merges those sufficient
statistics and centers once with the global mean. Centering each partition and averaging its
covariance generally loses between-partition terms. The supplied check compares the merge
result with an independently centered batch calculation on a crossed 63-row fixture; maximum
discrepancies are below 2 × 10−16 in this environment.
from causalbank import ScoreReducer

left = ScoreReducer(n_entities=10000, n_dates=120, dimension=2)
right = ScoreReducer(n_entities=10000, n_dates=120, dimension=2)
# Each worker adds disjoint rows of precomputed scores and integer keys.
left.add(score_part_a, entity_part_a, date_part_a)
right.add(score_part_b, entity_part_b, date_part_b)
result = left.merge(right).result()

The caller owns score construction, target weighting and the sampling assumptions. A raw
regression coefficient is not automatically a score. For a nonlinear estimating equation, its
Jacobian and normalization must be applied consistently. Unequal target weights need a
defined weighted score and denominator; they are not supplied by this prototype.
   The covariance can be indefinite in a finite sample. The reference reports its minimum
eigenvalue and a flag instead of silently forcing a positive matrix. A consumer must then use a
scientifically justified alternative or withhold the affected interval. The component also rejects
nonfinite scores, incompatible shapes and too few nonempty clusters. It does not choose a
bandwidth, bootstrap method or independent-unit definition for the analyst.
15.5. What the scale measurement actually times                                               89


15.5     What the scale measurement actually times
The scale fixture creates two-dimensional synthetic scores in chunks of 100,000 rows, with
10,000 declared entity keys and 120 date keys. Three fresh child processes run at each size.
The total timer includes score generation, accumulation and final covariance; the reduction
timer isolates accumulation. Linux peak resident memory includes the interpreter and loaded
libraries.

                       Rows Total seconds Reduce seconds Peak RSS (MiB)
                     100,000          0.098           0.078              78.0
                   1,000,000          0.232           0.133             115.2
                  10,000,000          1.208           0.641             123.0

Table 15.2: Median of three local runs per size. Precomputed-score reduction only: no storage
reads, temporal reconstruction, nuisance fitting, causal graph search or POMDP parameter
fitting is included.

   The measured ten-million-row operation takes about 1.2 seconds and 123 MiB peak resident
memory in this environment. These numbers show that a bounded score reduction can avoid
retaining all rows. They cannot be advertised as the latency of a ten-million-row causal
analysis. The dense intersection arrays require O((E + T + ET )d) score storage plus counts.
With ten million entities, even 120 dates makes that representation inappropriate. A sparse
grouped or warehouse aggregation is then required and must be measured separately. The
current measurement does not establish a universal streaming-memory bound independent of
cluster cardinality.
   The benchmark records Python and NumPy versions, platform and component hashes.
Shared-host load can change timing. There was no dedicated machine reservation, storage
benchmark or comparison with Ray. A production qualification should specify cores, memory
limits, execution concurrency, data format, warm/cold caches and complete stage costs before
committing to a service objective.


15.6     A reproducible job is a dependency graph
A compiled job should reference a frozen snapshot and a deterministic fold assignment. A
nuisance fit depends only on its training role. Score tasks depend on the exact model versions
and their evaluation partitions. Inference depends on the complete set of score partitions, with
declared target weights and covariance method. Report generation depends on the financial
account and both scientific and computational statuses.
   The artifact identity should hash canonical configuration, input manifest digests, code/de-
pendency lock identity and random seeds. A model upgrade, changed treatment mapping or
later outcome snapshot changes that identity. An authorization decision remains dynamic
even when content is immutable: a previously readable artifact may cease to be exportable
after a permission change. Content identity must not be confused with access authority.
  Retries require an exactly-once contribution rule. A failed worker may write the same score
partition twice; the manifest must select one committed artifact for that partition, rather
than summing both. Committing the partition manifest atomically is preferable to inferring
completion from the presence of a partially written file. A reducer starts only when all expected
partitions are present and valid.
  Checkpointing is method-specific. An EM checkpoint includes model parameters, iteration,
90                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


objective and sufficient-statistic configuration. A bootstrap checkpoint includes resample
identity and fit diagnostics. A graph-search checkpoint includes candidate constraints and
conditioning tests already performed. Resuming with changed data or constraints is a new
run. Saving an arbitrary Python process state is not the public reconstruction contract.


15.7      Three concrete repository adoption journeys
FinMarketing can export assignment episodes, decision-time covariates and a group contribution
ledger. The proposed integration reconstructs the snapshot, computes cohort effects and returns
joint balance/contribution uncertainty with an explicit target and sign. Acceptance compares
the same study with FinMarketing’s existing calculation and reconciles transfers account by
account.
   dataml can export a recovery ensemble with observed/missing masks, the measurement
model, draw identifiers and training partition provenance. The causal consumer repeats
the declared analysis under compatible draws and reports recovery sensitivity. The initial
integration should use an exact small corrupted-data fixture whose observed entries remain
unchanged. It fails if a recovered outcome is exposed as a historical policy feature or uncertainty
is lost when the ensemble becomes a dataframe.
   BayesFilter can supply a filtering or likelihood component through a narrow numerical
interface. A controlled model specifies whether the action factor enters its historical posterior
and when the reward is observed. Its probabilities and gradients are compared with exact
short-path sums before larger fits. The causal library retains ownership of the intervention
interpretation. MacroFinance can similarly consume response-path covariance and shock
restrictions; cardnpv additionally requires an explicit contrast direction conversion. These are
proposed acceptance journeys, not existing inter-repository calls.


15.8      Building the independent application
The standalone workbench should guide the bank user through subject and action selection,
eligibility, the decision-time account, design declaration, method comparison and economic
outcomes. Discovery should display ambiguous endpoints and measurements or interventions
that could distinguish them. Latent-state analysis should show filtering uncertainty, fit
diagnostics and conditional policy value, preserving its identification restrictions.
  The proposed SDK and evidence export should expose the operation records. The interface
should explain unsupported requests in the user’s terms: no untreated branches remain after
the last rollout date, or severe-state assistance was never observed. Worker identifiers and
dependency hashes belong in expandable technical evidence.
  A bank deployment should reuse identity, catalog, warehouse and storage services. Workers
execute near authorized data; the control service holds study metadata and permitted references.
Regional boundaries cover derived scores and fitted models as well as rows. R, Java and
Python adapters each require environment qualification and applicable license review.
   Release acceptance reconstructs an exported study in a clean qualified environment; detects
late-data, support and sign errors; resumes interrupted jobs without duplicate contributions;
and reconciles financial totals independently. Review-effort savings must then be measured on
equivalent tasks.

Evidence and validation

16.1     Different claims require different evidence
This proposal includes executable illustrations, preserved sources and checked specifications.
They demonstrate selected identities and interfaces, not estimator superiority, production
scale, institutional acceptance or a profitable bank intervention.
  Qualification distinguishes mathematical identity, implementation correctness, simulation
operating characteristics, real-data design validity, prospective economic value and operational
acceptance. Success at one level informs the next; it does not replace it.

The larger synthetic studies supply fitted estimation, financial accounting and adverse compar-

  The controlled-HMM verification enumerates all sixteen latent paths of short observed
sequences, with and without hidden-state action selection. It agrees with the scaled for-
ward/backward calculation for likelihood and initial, transition, emission and action expected
counts to below 4 × 10−15 . This is a check on the implementation’s probability factorization,
not a test that a bank satisfies it.
94                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   A separate three-decision collections enumeration sums 375 supported state/action paths.
The expanded DR score and a backward recursive calculation agree within 10−12 on those paths.
Expected scores equal the exact policy value when the action law or action value is correct;
the chosen both-wrong case has bias about USD 1.16. The current-ratio-only calculation has
expected value about negative USD 22.91 against true negative USD 13.66. This isolates a
target mismatch independently of the larger study’s Monte Carlo noise.
   The latent-model follow-up also extends the main capped optimization on the same data
and starting seeds. It preserves the sign reversal from omitting the action mechanism. The
thirty-repetition comparison remains a finite-budget experiment, with caps explicitly reported.
An optimizer stopping test is not a global-optimum certificate.




16.2.2    What still requires bank qualification

Vary outcome noise, treatment imbalance, support, hidden confounding, serial/cross-sectional
dependence, informative missingness, regimes, interference and horizon. Generate truth
separately from observed data; prevent estimators and tuners from accessing oracle states or
counterfactuals. Freeze evaluation scenarios before comparison.
   For effects, compare regression, IPW, g-computation, orthogonal/targeted methods and
justified neural challengers. Report bias, RMSE, coverage, interval width, unsupported cases,
abstention and subgroup behavior. A method that reports a confident point effect in an
unidentified scenario should fail the scientific test even if optimization succeeds.
   Panel cases include heterogeneous effects, staggered/reversible treatment, anticipation, trend
violations, few clusters and spillovers. POMDP cases vary emission overlap, state dimension,
private logging information, support, horizon, misspecification and state aliasing. Assess
predictive fit, parameter recovery up to labels, value error and conservative decisions.
   Discovery benchmarks require latent causes, contemporaneous relations, nonstationarity,
missingness and aggregation. Score adjacency and endpoints against the correct equivalence-
class target. Structural Hamming distance alone can reward unjustified orientation or penalize
justified uncertainty. Include downstream identification and intervention-prediction tests.

p An initial 500-replication coverage study has Monte Carlo standard error about
   0.95(0.05)/500 = 0.00975 at true 95% coverage. A 92–98% observed coverage band
is a proposed smoke criterion, not a guarantee. Report Monte Carlo intervals, diagnose
systematic failures, and increase replication when decision precision warrants it.




16.3     Reference agreement and adverse cases

Adapters should reproduce exact small cases and independent reference implementations within
stated tolerances. Exact finite calculations permit tight tolerances; stochastic optimization
requires a different comparison.
   Adverse tests include backdated features, duplicate entities, policy changes, all-treated
strata, missing propensities, outcome leakage, receipt substituted for assignment, lost graph
marks, sign reversal and mixed currency. Test interruption/retry equivalence and full artifact
reconstruction. Return typed limitations rather than invent missing information.
16.4. Real-bank validation and experiments                                                   95


16.4     Real-bank validation and experiments
Begin with an existing randomized study and a rollout already understood by bank economists.
Reconstruct the original clocks, population and analysis; compare results and review ef-
fort. Then conduct a prospective study with prespecified financial/customer outcomes and
institutionally appropriate interventions.
  For a balanced two-arm experiment with total independent sample n, common standard
deviation σ and effect ∆, rough planning gives

                                       4σ 2 (z1−α/2 + z1−β )2
                                  n≈                          .
                                                 ∆2
At σ = 100, ∆ = 5, α = 0.05 and 80% power this is about 12,550 units before attrition,
clustering or multiple outcomes. The equal-cluster design-effect approximation is 1 + (m − 1)ρ
for mean cluster size m and intracluster correlation ρ; unequal clusters require more specific
calculation. These are illustrations, not bank sample-size commitments.
   Compare matched workflow tasks on time to valid cohort, successful replay, material findings,
cost and decision relevance. A proposed target is 30% lower median analyst/reviewer effort
without more unresolved material findings. Establish baseline variability and task complexity
first. This target is a sponsor hypothesis to test.


16.5     Value, uncertainty and customer outcomes
Policy comparisons include contribution, loss, liquidity, capacity and relevant customer out-
comes. Requirements and thresholds belong to the institution’s decision process. Examine
subgroup uncertainty, access, support and error consequences. Predictive fairness metrics do
not establish causal fairness or legal permissibility.
  Separate sampling, identification, model and economic-input uncertainty. A credible interval
conditional on a structural prior is not an identified set. A downstream optimizer must receive
the distinction explicitly. Use sensitivity ranges alongside statistical intervals rather than
compressing every uncertainty source into an unjustified single number.


16.6     Release acceptance
Acceptance requires working workflows, replayable studies, qualified dependencies, bank-data
authorization, model validation and operational ownership. Independent model validation is a
future activity, distinct from this author’s review and synthetic calculations.
   Stop or narrow a module when variation is absent, support fails, intervals are miscalibrated,
a simpler reference performs better at lower cost, or value cannot justify complexity. A not
identified result can usefully motivate an experiment; it is not a failed software job.
Chapter 17

The economic case for a shared
product

17.1     Compare the same scientific work
The credible alternative is a capable internal team using its warehouse, catalog, versioned
notebooks and established open-source packages. That team can implement the methods
surveyed here. The proposed product must justify the extra expense of reusable semantics,
interfaces and operations through repeated use, lower review effort or additional decision
value. Its comparison cannot assume that the alternative omits temporal correctness, credible
controls or model validation.
   Define a completed study as a decision with a frozen population and information clock, a
stated target, defensible identifying restrictions, at least one suitable reference comparison,
an economic account and a reconstructible evidence package. Both alternatives must deliver
the same number and mix of such studies, with equivalent scientific review. The platform
automates recurring work; expert composition performs more of it in study-specific code and
procedures. Neither is entitled to count unreviewed model fits as completed studies.
   The cost account has initial common construction Kj , annual shared operation Fjt and
incremental study cost cjk for alternative j. Study cost includes analyst, engineering and review
effort, allocated compute and recurring data reconciliation. Shared cost includes dependency
qualification, orchestration, support, security and reusable validation. An existing bank catalog
is a common baseline input; a new connection required by one alternative is an incremental
cost of that alternative.


17.2     The reuse threshold
For nt equivalent completed studies in year t, present cost is

17.3. Illustrative costs, including losing scenarios                                            97


The numerator is its annualized common-cost premium; the denominator is the saving per
completed equivalent study. If ∆c ≤ 0 and common-cost premiums are positive, reuse alone
cannot justify the platform. No amount of repeating an equally expensive workflow removes
that premium.
   Heterogeneous studies need the original sum in Equation (17.1). A new country’s undocu-
mented action logs may require nearly as much work with either stack. A twentieth deposit
rollout over a qualified data account may reuse most of its transformation and review evidence.
Counting both as identical use cases would inflate the expected saving.


17.3      Illustrative costs, including losing scenarios
Use a three-year horizon and 10% discount rate. All amounts in this section are illustrative
USD millions. Expert composition requires initial common work of 1.0, annual shared cost
0.6 and 0.15 per completed study. The product requires 4.0 initially, 1.8 annually and 0.06
per study. These are planning assumptions to be replaced by a bank estimate. They are not
observed salary rates, procurement prices or measured productivity.
   The study-cost difference is 0.09 million. At the separate staffing assumption of USD 25,000
per person-month, that is 3.6 person-months saved per completed study. That is a large claim:
it must be demonstrated on equivalent tasks, not inferred from the existence of a common
API. The product’s annual shared cost includes support and dependency work; study-specific
engineering and review are included in its per-study cost. The categories must not overlap.

                    Scenario          Expert cost Platform cost Platform saving
                    Low reuse               5.476        9.670           -4.194
                    Moderate reuse         11.445       12.057           -0.613
                    High reuse             15.921       13.848            2.073
                    Adoption ramp           8.402       10.840           -2.438

Table 17.1: Three-year present cost in illustrative USD millions. Constant annual volumes are
8, 24 and 36 studies; the ramp is 4, 16 and 30. Positive saving favors the shared product.

   The cost-only threshold is about 26.74 completed studies per year. At eight annually the
product costs about USD 4.19 million more in present value. At 24 it still costs about USD 0.61
million more. At 36 it saves about USD 2.07 million. An adoption ramp of 4, 16 and 30
studies leaves a USD 2.44 million premium even though final-year throughput exceeds the
constant-volume threshold. Early costs occur before much reuse.
   If the per-study saving is half as large, the threshold doubles to about 53.47 studies annually.
If the annual shared-cost premium rises from 1.2 to 2.0 million, the original per-study saving
needs about 35.63 studies annually. These sensitivities argue for measuring reusable effort
early and keeping common construction narrow until multiple teams use it. A platform built
for imagined reuse can be economically worse than a well-maintained expert toolkit.

Let Dt be additional realized business value attributable to the product relative to the equivalent

The first term already counts workflow cost savings. Do not add the same released analyst
time again as a separate business benefit. If that time supports additional studies, model their
costs and incremental decisions explicitly, with a capacity constraint.
  At 24 studies per year the illustrative cost premium requires about USD 0.246 million of
additional constant annual decision benefit. For the adoption ramp it requires about USD 0.980
million. Those may be modest amounts for a large banking group, but group size is not
evidence that the product creates them. The expert comparator may already find the same
beneficial intervention. An analyst’s higher point estimate is not realized incremental value.
  The deposit study gives a useful distinction. Discovering that a promotion loses contribution
can avoid an expansion loss, but the prevented loss is attributable only if the comparator
would otherwise expand it and the finding changes the decision. The collections simulation’s
positive policy gain is a property of its generating model; it supplies no bank revenue for
Equation (17.3). A hidden-state module may have positive research value while its operational
policy benefit remains unresolved.
   Risk reduction is also a counterfactual claim. If the platform catches a late-data feature,
record its frequency, review disposition and consequence under the baseline process. Do not
multiply an arbitrary low-probability catastrophe by a large bank balance sheet and call the
result a measured benefit. Early validation can instead report concrete errors detected and
the cost of resolving them.


17.5                                         Adoption, maturity and cash timing
Not every initiated study reaches a usable conclusion. A simple planning decomposition is

                                                             nusable
                                                              t      = nstarted
                                                                        t       pdata
                                                                                 t    pdesign
                                                                                       t      pcompleted
                                                                                               t         preview
                                                                                                          t      ,

where the probabilities are conditional progression rates, not assumed independent events.
The multiplicative form is the chain rule when each rate conditions on prior progression. Costs
incurred by failed studies remain in the account. A well-designed product may appropriately
terminate more unidentified studies early; usable throughput should then be assessed alongside
avoided futile effort.
17.6. Measuring the product hypothesis in the first tranche                                   99


  Decision outcomes mature later still. A six-month deposit outcome can become observable
within a pilot year; losses from a credit-limit change may take longer. A continuing value
model introduces assumptions rather than making those outcomes observed. Discounting
should follow the actual date of expenditure and realized benefit, with distinct data-access,
development, study and outcome lags.
  The earlier aggregate illustration can be retained as a stress calculation: a USD 4 million
outlay and USD 1.8 million annual operation cost need constant annual incremental benefit of
approximately USD 3.408 million over three years at 10%. At USD 5 million annual benefit its
NPV is USD 3.958 million; losing the first year’s benefit makes it about negative USD 0.588
million. Those values use a coarser account than the equal-output comparison and must not
be added to it. The explicit comparator model is the preferred investment account.


17.6      Measuring the product hypothesis in the first tranche

Choose a small set of matched tasks across the three workspaces: reconstruct a rollout, evaluate
a repeated-decision policy under a defensible design, and organize a temporal discovery dataset
with known semantic ambiguities. Agree their required outputs and reviewer rubric before
timing them. Give the expert-composition arm the same source access, compute budget and
scientific expertise. It may reuse its own sensible templates.
   Measure active analyst and reviewer hours separately from calendar delay, data-owner
response time and machine time. Record task complexity, previous familiarity, failed starts,
rework and unresolved material findings. A counterbalanced assignment of comparable tasks
can reduce learning-order effects; repeated use by several teams is necessary to estimate reuse
rather than first-author familiarity. A proposed target of 30% lower median analyst/reviewer
effort is an investment hypothesis, not a result already established by this proposal.
   The platform should also export a study to a second analyst who did not author it. Measure
time to reproduce the target, source account and financial conclusion, and whether the analyst
notices deliberately introduced temporal, support or sign errors. Equivalent review quality is
part of the output definition. Faster execution with more unrecognized scientific defects is not
a saving.
   The first tranche is six people for six months: one product/economics lead, two causal/econo-
metric scientists, two data/platform engineers and one application engineer. At the illustrative
loaded rate, staffing is USD 900,000; compute/tooling USD 50,000 and 20% contingency bring
the total to USD 1.14 million. That tranche is included within the illustrative USD 4 million
platform construction, not added to it. Bank-owner, independent-validation and security
participation remain unpriced and must be estimated consistently for both alternatives before
funding.
  Six people cannot production-qualify every method in the census in six months. They can
construct the common account and evidence layer, qualify a narrow panel/longitudinal path,
and deliver finite-state estimation and temporal discovery as explicit research capabilities. The
next investment depends on observed scientific usefulness and reusable effort rather than on
completing a broad feature checklist.


17.7      Independent product economics and procurement

An independent offering adds customer-specific deployment, support, upgrades, contracts and
onboarding costs. Code reuse does not eliminate each institution’s semantic mapping and
100                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


validation. A plausible initial commercial form is a design-partner deployment with a paid
construction scope and recurring support, preserving SDK and evidence export. Willingness
to pay, sales cycle, support load and customer concentration have not been measured here.
   Compare a commercial vendor on the same reconstructed studies, permission boundaries,
supported identification routes, exported uncertainty and dependency responsibilities. Vendor
demos and list prices are insufficient; no current private enterprise capability or price is asserted
in this survey. For internal adoption, chargeback should distinguish common capability from a
business unit’s bespoke model so that demand is not inflated by unpriced customization.
   The sponsor’s decision is therefore conditional but concrete: fund a narrow shared construc-
tion if named teams have repeatable decisions, reconstructible data and a credible path to
reusable work. Continue expert composition where volume is low or assumptions differ too
much. Expand the common product when measured study cost, quality and adoption support
the incremental account. The financial case becomes stronger through evidence of actual reuse,
not through assigning all of a bank’s causal-analysis benefit to a new software layer.
Chapter 18

Delivery, ownership and stopping
decisions

18.1      Develop the central capabilities together
The initial program develops three workspaces: policy and transmission, sequential decisions
with controlled latent-state estimation, and temporal discovery with automatic data organiza-
tion. They share a temporal account, study semantics and evidence system. Their scientific
claims mature at different rates. A useful first POMDP module can estimate a declared model
and display conditional policy scenarios; a discovery module can return ambiguous endpoints
and candidate experiments. Neither needs to claim that observational data uniquely identify
every intervention.
   The first six-month tranche funds a small common implementation and bounded application
paths. It should qualify a narrow panel/longitudinal analysis, an inspectable finite-state
estimation path and a temporal discovery adapter. It should not attempt production support
for all 44 surveyed projects. The illustrative USD 1.14 million team and the equal-output
economic comparator are developed in Chapter 17; future funding depends on observed reuse
and scientific usefulness.

   The first month is substantive design work. For deposits, identify which branches changed
policy, whether customers anticipated it, whether external funds can be distinguished from
internal transfers and whether untreated comparisons remain. For collections, inspect how staff
discretion and unrecorded information entered actions. For discovery, define the frequency,
measurement coverage and admissible contemporaneous relationships before choosing a graph
algorithm. A warehouse extract without these answers does not make a model ready.
   The next stage implements one end-to-end path before generalizing. A cohort study is
reconstructed from original events, fitted with a reference comparison and exported with
target weights and contribution uncertainty. The latent-state path starts with the exact
count/likelihood checks in Chapter 7; the discovery path preserves equivalence classes and
assumptions. These paths exercise common components under different scientific demands
and reveal which abstractions are truly reusable.
   By month six the platform should support another analyst repeating a bounded study
without help from its author. That is a stronger acceptance condition than a polished
first-author demo. A research-only state remains appropriate for a module without a bank
identifying design. The bank may continue useful data and scenario work while funding a
measurement or randomization plan to answer the unresolved causal question.


18.3      Who owns each decision
The business owner specifies the action, feasible comparator, economic account and decision
threshold. The data owner attests to historical coverage, identity and timestamp semantics.
The science owner signs the identification argument, estimator and inference design. The
engineering owner signs computational reproducibility, access and operation. Independent
model validation challenges the complete analysis under the institution’s applicable framework.
None of these roles is replaced by a successful schema check.
  Changes have different approval and requalification consequences within the future bank
process. A documentation correction may leave a result unchanged. A changed funds-transfer
price changes the economic scenario. A new treatment definition or population changes the
18.4. Qualification gates with concrete failure outcomes                                       103


estimand. A package upgrade can alter covariance defaults or missing-value handling. The
study record should show which objects changed and which previous evidence still applies,
rather than carrying forward one undifferentiated approval.
   The shared product owner maintains supported combinations and deprecation policy. An
adapter version can remain available for historical replay while being barred from new decision
use after a material defect. Historical reports should identify the affected dependency and
receive an attached notice; they should not be silently rewritten as if the corrected result had
always been known.


18.4      Qualification gates with concrete failure outcomes
A data gate fails if the requested decision-time account cannot be reconstructed, material
transfers do not reconcile, or missing coverage is mistaken for zero. The response is a corrected
source mapping, a narrower population or a data-collection plan. It is not permission to use a
final warehouse view as if it were historically available.
   An identification gate fails if no adequate treatment variation or proxy, instrument, random-
ization or structural route is available. The response can be an identified set, a conditional
scenario or a proposed experiment. The product can still report useful information, but it
cannot label the result an identified point effect. A discovery graph or predictive latent fit
alone cannot waive this gate.
   An estimation gate fails if the declared method does not fit the data shape, overlap is
insufficient for the intended intervention, numerical fits are unstable or relevant simulated
intervals are badly miscalibrated. The response may be a shorter policy horizon, a supported
intervention, a simpler estimator or an explicit unresolved result. Weight clipping, state
aggregation and policy restriction change the analysis and must be shown as such.
   An economic gate fails if contribution definitions are incompatible, uncertainty crosses the
decision threshold, or the product’s added cost is not justified against expert composition. A
scientifically valid null finding can still save the bank from a poor action. It does not establish
that an expensive shared platform is the cheapest way to obtain that finding. Module and
platform decisions therefore have separate accounts.
   An operational gate fails if another authorized user cannot reconstruct the evidence, if
retries duplicate contributions, if regional access is violated or if dependency ownership is
absent. The resolution is an engineering or operating change. Such defects should not be
hidden inside a scientific sensitivity interval.


18.5      Prospective learning and model maintenance
A prospective pilot should compare a small prespecified set of feasible strategies, with economic
and customer outcomes, a horizon and stopping rules agreed in advance. Policy learning must
respect a held-out evaluation or a suitable selection-adjusted design. An attractive fitted value
from the same data used to optimize the policy is insufficient evidence of improvement.
   Monitoring separates population change, assignment change, observation change and re-
sponse change. A rise in missed measurements can change a latent-state likelihood; a new
staff override process can change action selection; an interest-rate regime can change deposit
response. A common alert on prediction error does not diagnose all three. The model record
should link each alert to the affected assumption and evidence needed for continued use.
  Outcome maturity affects monitoring as well as economics. Early repayment can be observed
104                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


before ultimate losses; closing an account can end product balance records without ending its
group-level economic outcome. A status page should distinguish complete computation from
mature outcomes and future-value assumptions. This makes a study useful before lifetime
results arrive without misrepresenting what has been learned.


18.6     Research priorities that change delivery choices
The highest-value research reduces a specific uncertainty in a banking application: whether
private logging can be measured, whether weak proxies support stable policy value, whether
common-shock inference is calibrated, or whether a proposed discovery restriction survives
aggregation. Each research ticket should state the competing constructions, an observable
failure criterion and the product decision it changes.
  Chapter 19 discusses current research through the survey cutoff. Foundation models
and automated semantic systems are candidates for reducing fitting or organization effort,
not assumed replacements for identification. Hidden-state, irregular-time and nonstationary
methods remain central research from the beginning, with release claims limited to the evidence
actually obtained.
   The practical stopping rule is modular. Keep a useful temporal account, panel workflow
or conditional latent-model workbench when another module fails its causal or economic
qualification. Stop expanding a shared layer when each additional application requires bespoke
work that erases the assumed reuse saving. Expand when multiple teams can reconstruct useful
studies at acceptable cost and quality with a clear owner for every scientific and operational
claim.
Chapter 19

Current research and unresolved
product choices

19.1     A new method must change a decision

Recent research matters when it changes a feasible estimand, required measurement, uncertainty
calculation or computational cost. Publication recency alone is not a reason to replace a
qualified estimator. The survey cutoff is 7 October 2026; several cited 2026 works are recent
preprints, including one posted the preceding day. Their archived versions and provisional
status are retained in the source register. None has been runtime-qualified on bank records in
this commission.
   The central unresolved questions cut across method families. Can the bank identify the
information used by its historical decision maker? Can it distinguish a customer response
from a common economic shock? Does a measurement arrive because risk increased? Does a
fitted latent model preserve the response when policy changes? Does a faster estimator merely
move untested assumptions into its training prior? These questions determine the useful role
of current research.


19.2     Amortized inference moves work into a prior

Prior-data fitted networks train on many synthetic datasets and learn a mapping from a new
dataset to an approximate posterior or estimator. If successful for a supported task, this can
reduce repeated tuning and fitting cost. Let Π be a prior over observational/interventional
model pairs and Q a causal query. The learned approximation targets a prior-conditional
object such as
                                   Z
                     Π(Q | D) ∝        1{Q(M ) ∈ dQ} p(D | M ) Π(dM ).

The model family and its identifying restrictions enter before observing the bank dataset.
Approximation to this posterior is a computational achievement; it does not verify that the
prior’s exclusion or invariance restrictions hold for that bank.
   The inspected ICLR 2026 CausalFM paper makes identification an explicit input, including
declared backdoor, frontdoor and instrumental-variable settings (Ma et al., 2026). Its Section
3 defines an identified query as a functional of the observational law on the maintained model
class. This distinction is valuable for the product: an amortized estimator can sit behind the
same design contract as a conventional estimator. It does not infer a valid instrument from a

                                             105
106                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


column’s predictive usefulness. The archived work is CausalFM, distinct from the concurrent
CausalPFN work it discusses.
   Consider two models with the same observed distribution but different intervention effects,
as constructed in Chapter 6. Their likelihood ratio remains one for every observational sample.
Posterior odds between them therefore remain prior odds. A network cannot learn a uniformly
correct effect from that same observed law without additional restrictions or information. If
its prior excludes one model, a narrow posterior is conditional on that exclusion. A reliability
head trained to recognize simulated regimes inherits the same boundary.
   The temporal PFN preprint describes temporal tokens, a causal-judgment head, context
selection and posterior correction (Talupula and Sharma, 2026). These are interesting can-
didates for reducing repeated computation and prioritizing uncertain analyses. The stated
source does not establish that an inferred identifiability score is a mathematical certificate
for an arbitrary banking panel. Its industrial examples also have different measurement and
action processes from endogenous bank pricing or relationship-manager discretion.
   Qualification should hold out entire generating mechanisms, not merely new draws from
the training generator. Include weak instruments, proxy exclusion violations, hidden policy
changes, long shared shocks and delayed revisions absent from the synthetic prior. Compare
effects and interval calibration with conventional estimators on the same target; measure
context selection and preprocessing as well as inference time. For an amortized product,
pretraining and upgrade cost belongs in the economic account even when per-study fitting is
fast.



19.3     Proximal learning: the inverse problem survives automa-
         tion

The ProximalFM preprint, posted on 6 October 2026, explicitly adopts latent exchangeability,
proxy exclusions, latent positivity and completeness; it additionally assumes conditions for an
outcome bridge to exist (Muller et al., 2026, Sections 2.1–2.2). It predicts a CATE posterior
from synthetic proximal models instead of solving a new bridge optimization for each dataset.
The target averages over proxies conditional on the designated covariates X.
   Those roles have concrete banking meaning. A candidate treatment-inducing proxy must
carry information about hidden risk without violating the outcome exclusion once action and
the latent causes are held fixed. An outcome-inducing proxy must satisfy its own conditional
independence from action and the first proxy. A staff assessment that directly changes both
assistance and later follow-up may violate these restrictions. More predictive proxy variables
are not automatically better identifying measurements.
    In the finite bridge calculation, small singular values of the relevant conditional-probability
matrix amplify estimation noise. In a functional bridge, the corresponding operator can be
ill posed. Regularization trades bias and instability under a chosen function class (Ghassami
et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2024). Amortization may encode a useful regularizer through its prior,
but does not remove the need to examine weak-proxy and prior-sensitivity cases. The bank
should receive value sensitivity and unsupported conditions alongside any fast point estimate.
  The product research question is therefore whether a specified proxy measurement design
supports useful policy precision. A promising next experiment can collect an additional
pre-action measurement under a known process, compare candidate bridges and test value
sensitivity. Calling every transaction-derived embedding a proxy would evade the scientific
problem rather than solve it.
19.4. Coverage at one date can hide long-horizon difficulty                                  107


19.4      Coverage at one date can hide long-horizon difficulty

Positive action probabilities at each date are necessary for many off-policy estimators but
can leave target trajectories extremely rare. The collections study demonstrates weight
concentration even with conditional randomization. Markov occupancy-ratio estimators can
improve efficiency when the state representation and sampling restrictions support their
factorization (Kallus and Uehara, 2020). A compressed learned state must retain the relevant
information before that argument can be used.
   A recent hardness preprint constructs exponentially difficult evaluation with an unconfounded
history-dependent logger, a deterministic memoryless target and favorable behavior-marginal
coverage quantities (Jajoo, 2026, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 4.1). Its result concerns a specific
model class and definitions of revealing/coverage. It does not imply that every bank POMDP
is exponentially difficult. It does refute an overly broad product claim that good one-step
coverage metrics alone establish easy long-horizon evaluation.
  This suggests a hierarchy of proposed outputs: short prespecified policy contrasts where
support is adequate, model-conditional longer scenarios, and learning designs that deliberately
improve information about the target policy. Report where the policy’s history distribution
departs from observed experience. A large total transaction count can coexist with little
evidence on the sequence needed for a decision.


19.5      Partial identification needs a temporal confounding model

When point identification fails, bounds can still help choose among actions. But a dynamic
bound cannot be assembled from arbitrary independently chosen local worst cases if those
choices cannot coexist within one underlying process. The shape of the uncertainty set matters.
  The inspected sharp-dynamic-bounds preprint restricts unmeasured confounding to act
within a stage and not persist as a hidden state into later stages (Alvarez and Ferrando,
2026). Its local feasible transition sets then combine under the stated temporal restrictions,
supporting a backward robust evaluation. Persistent wealth, financial fragility or relationship
quality in banking can violate precisely that restriction. The two-state process in Chapter 7 is
an example where persistence is central rather than an incidental nuisance.
   The product should therefore distinguish bounds from stage-local confounding, sensitivity
sets for a persistent latent model and history-based longitudinal restrictions. Each has its own
target and attainability argument. A visually wider interval does not automatically contain all
plausible bank mechanisms. An optimization routine finding extreme values within a declared
set establishes only that conditional calculation.


19.6      Irregular observations are often informative

Bank records have irregular calls, document requests and account activity. Regularizing them
to a monthly grid changes the measurement process. The ITSY preprint couples completion
and temporal graph estimation, with its displayed setup assuming causal sufficiency, stationary
mechanisms and MCAR missingness; its implemented structural model uses first-order lags
(Xu et al., 2026, Section 3). Those restrictions give a clear comparator domain. They also
exclude many risk-triggered measurement processes that a banking product must represent
explicitly.
  For example, a customer contacted after deteriorating arrears is more likely to provide
108                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


an updated income measure. The absence of that measure is then informative about the
underlying process or policy. A completion algorithm that treats the gaps as independent
can alter both contemporaneous and lagged associations. Discovery must model or restrict
observation selection, or return a limitation, before interpreting the completed graph.
   Continuous-time causal SDE work provides another language for interventions, with existence,
solvability and structural requirements (Boeken and Mooij, 2026). A mathematical intervention
construction does not by itself supply an estimator for irregular bank logs. A bank pilot must
specify the sampling process, what action operates between observations and which parameters
are recoverable at that frequency.
  Other recent proposals use spectral signatures to route corrections for different confounding
patterns, accelerate temporal conditional-independence tests, or constrain discovery through
group-level background knowledge (Fesanghary, 2026b,a; Ruiz de Vargas et al., 2026). They
motivate explicit challengers. Their reported speed or graph improvements were not reproduced
here, and background constraints remain substantive assumptions.


19.7     The research portfolio has measurable exits
Each research line should end in a product decision. An amortized estimator earns an adapter
when it improves equivalent-task cost with acceptable calibration under relevant mechanism
shifts. A proxy method earns a policy-value claim when a defensible measurement design and
stability analysis support it. A discovery extension earns use when its graph semantics and
observation assumptions match the bank’s records. A latent model earns a planning role when
its causal route, numerical fit and decision uncertainty are adequate for the proposed action.
   The negative outcomes are useful too: retain a conventional estimator, collect better
measurements, shorten a policy horizon, report a set or use discovery to plan an intervention.
This portfolio treats new methods as competing solutions to bank questions. It avoids
committing the independent product to a promise that the next model architecture will
eliminate identification, dependence or data-semantic work.
Appendix A

Research protocol and source
concordance

A.1     Coverage and provenance

The local inventory contains 7,891 PDFs across the user’s library and the FinMarketing paper
folder. Discovery used Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv, proceedings, author copies and official
repositories. It retained 64 public search requests: 59 saved and five failed. These yielded
457 unique normalized-title candidates. The final census includes 415 total registered public
requests. Counts describe collected records, not all literature.
   This is a purposive review. Sources were selected when they changed an assumption,
estimator, failure mode, banking design, software choice or requirement. Recent searches
covered 2024 through 7 October 2026; foundational work had no date restriction. Preprints
retain explicit version labels. The banking-specific survey (Kumar et al., 2023) supplies
discovery leads; primary papers support substantive claims.
   Every cited scholarly work has a real local PDF named by title, first-author surname and
citation year. The register records the actual archived version, which may be a working
manuscript corresponding to a later publication. Original titles remain in metadata when
prohibited filename punctuation is removed. Three official guidance PDFs are also preserved.
Software citations refer to manifests whose component documents have content hashes.
   Records include sources, reading notes, claims, search/request ledgers, candidates, metadata
audit, software assessment, local-repository snapshots and omissions. The concordance maps
citation keys to identities; an HTML index opens the saved PDFs. Hashes detect file changes
but do not establish scientific correctness.


A.2     Integrity repairs and access limits

Local filenames were treated as hints. A file labeled as a classic dynamic-panel-bias paper
contained a different work and was excluded. The liquidity-shock working paper is from 2006
and lists Mian first; the later publication’s reversed author order and year were not applied
to that copy. A mortgage-refinancing filename dated 2023 contained an April 2020 revision.
Guessed arXiv identifiers that resolved to unrelated papers were retained as raw excluded
downloads and replaced only after identity verification.
  The expanded 2025 ACM banking survey was located in metadata but its PDF was
inaccessible. The 2023 precursor is labeled accordingly. A 2023 Nature Reviews time-series

                                             109
110                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


review was not acquired and is not cited. An unavailable recurrent marginal structural-network
candidate is recorded as an omission; accessible primary longitudinal sources support the
chapter.
  Exact normalized-title metadata matches were available for 27 selected papers in the saved
corpus. Available update/retraction fields and citation counts are preserved. This is not
complete publisher, Crossmark or retraction-database clearance. Citation counts and venues
were not used as evidence of correctness.
   Coverage is strongest for effects, panels, longitudinal methods, partial observation, tem-
poral discovery and infrastructure. It is less comprehensive for continuous-time econometric
identification, network interference, transportability, online experiments and all jurisdictions’
requirements. Those limits constrain the claims.


A.3        Reconstruction and evidence classes

The source catalog rebuilds bibliography and records from copies and notes. The example
runner regenerates numerical outputs and figures. Contract examples contain hashes of the
frozen numerical artifact; regeneration requires deliberate refresh of those links. Contract
checks, document compilation and source/consistency audits complete the reconstruction.
  Document builds do not download sources. Public acquisition uses the separately approved
bounded collector. Saved receipts include failures and dates. Original PDFs and metadata
remain available offline.
   The author review examined mathematics, evidence boundaries, interfaces, citations and
rendered layout. It is not independent validation. Bank validation, third-party package runtime
qualification and full platform implementation remain future obligations. The two narrow
research components and executed synthetic studies are described separately in the main text.

      Symbol           Meaning
      i, t             Entity/trajectory and decision/calendar time
      At , Lt , Ht     Action, pre-action covariates and recorded history
      Y (a), Y g       Outcome under fixed action or policy
      et , gt , πt     Behavior assignment, intervention law and target policy
      Qt , Vt , Wt     Action value, policy-averaged value and cumulative importance
                       ratio
      St , Ot , bt     Latent state, available observation and filtered belief
      P, B, F, µ       Transition, emission, reward and initial-state distributions
      Gi , ATT(g, t)   Adoption date and group-time effect on treated
      θ, τ (x)         Population and conditional average effects
      C0 , Ot , Bt     Build cost, operating cost and benefit in the economics chapter; Bt
                       there is not an emission


   The introductory examples use synthetic currency units. The larger banking studies and
investment accounts explicitly use illustrative USD, with balance tables labeled in millions
where applicable. Real studies require currency, valuation date, horizon and sign.
